title: Public API Suite PRD and Launch Playbook for Generative Endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This PRD + playbook defines requirements, acceptance criteria, and the go-live checklist for Redwood's public API surface for generative endpoints: Completions, Chat, Embeddings, and Rerank. Goal is to ship a consistent, backwards-compatible, production-ready hosted API that supports streaming, function/tool calling for chat, configurable model selection, quota controls, and observability hooks required by customers migrating from early preview APIs.

Goals:
- Provide a single, well-documented API suite for typical LLM use cases with production SLAs.
- Ensure predictable latency and cost controls via documented batching, cache, and model suggestions.
- Offer straightforward upgrade path for early customers and partners with minimal client changes.
- Provide strong telemetry and regression detection tied to prompt/eval sets.

Non-goals / Out of scope:
- Dedicated-only deployment features (Reserved capacity autoscaling rules) — covered by Dedicated roadmap.
- In-depth on-prem installer (Private) packaging; only API contract and behavior documented.

Core user flows & requirements (high level):
1) Completions: single-turn text generation endpoint supporting temperature/top_p, stop tokens, max_tokens, logprobs optional, async job mode for very long outputs. Must support streaming.
2) Chat: multi-turn structured messages API with optional function/tool call surface, streaming delta tokens, per-message role enforcement and context length negotiation.
3) Embeddings: batched embeddings with per-item metadata passthrough, deterministic versioning, and configurable dimensionality for new models.
4) Rerank: take a query+candidate set and return ranked candidates + scores, stable tie-breaking, and optional explainability tokens.

API contract highlights (consumer-facing):
- Consistent error model (429, 500, 502, 503) with structured retry headers (Retry-After) and machine-friendly codes.
- Streaming uses SSE over the same endpoint; chunks may be re-ordered by network but must respect token ordering semantics.
- Delta events for function calls: START_CALL, CALL_ARG_CHUNK, END_CALL.
- Versioning: model param accepts exact model-id; fallback policy documented in headers (X-Model-Fallback).
- Quotas & rate limits: per-token and per-request quotas surfaced via response headers (X-Quota-Remaining, X-Per-Minute).

Backward compatibility & migration guidance:
- Provide compatibility shim for legacy preview SDKs for two cycles post-launch.
- Document common client changes in migration guide (consolidated parameters, streaming differences).

Operational requirements:
- End-to-end latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms for embeddings small batch (<=8, 512-d), P95 <= 500ms for short completions (<=128 tokens) on default model in us-west region.
- Error budget and alerting: integration with Console tracing; alerts for 5% error rate sustained >15m.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency.

Security & compliance:
- All endpoints must honor tenant isolation and do not leak prompts across tenants.
- Integrate with KMS for optional customer-managed keys.
- Require security review before GA (see security_review_required).

Acceptance criteria and launch gates are enumerated separately below.
acceptance_criteria: API contract finalized and published: OpenAPI + SDK examples (JS, Python) available in docs.redwood.ai
All endpoints pass contract tests including error codes, streaming event sequences, and quota headers
Performance SLOs met in staging for baseline workload (embedding batch 8x512, completions 128 tokens, chat context 4 messages) with automated benchmarks recorded
End-to-end integration tests validating function/tool calling across streaming and non-streaming paths
Security review completed and any critical/high findings remediated
Telemetry: dashboards created in Console for per-route latency, token cost, cache hit rate, and model fallback counts
Rate limit and quota headers implemented and validated with client throttling simulation
Migration docs and compatibility shim published; at least two early customers completed migration runbook
E2E load test: sustain expected median QPS for target initial GA cohort with <1% 5xx errors during a 1-hour soak
Launch checklist items below completed and validated by PM, Eng, and DevEx sign-offs
launch_checklist: Docs: API reference, quickstarts (JS/Python), migration guide, and changelog published
SDKs: release tagged versions with compatibility notes; smoke tests passing on npm/pypi
Console: route-level dashboards provisioned, SLO alerts wired to PagerDuty runbooks
Billing: per-token pricing configured in billing engine; test invoices generated for sample usage
Quota: soft and hard quotas configured with default thresholds for self-serve accounts
Security: KMS integration smoke test, tenant isolation integration test, and final security sign-off
Monitoring: synthetic traffic jobs in prod mimic GA flows (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
Rollout plan: dark launch 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated health checks
Canary kill-switch: documented rollback steps and automated policy to fall back to previous API surface
Support: playbook for triage with PS/Support including known issues and escalation paths
Legal & Compliance: Data residency notices updated; DPA addendum templates available for enterprise requests
Performance: documented model recommendations and quantization guidelines to achieve target unit cost
Customer comms: blog post draft, release notes, in-app banner schedule, and partner outreach list
updates: 2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Created PRD skeleton after scoping workshops with Eng and DevEx. Captured initial SLO targets and draft API contract.
2025-02-14 - Arjun Patel: Eng feedback: clarify streaming event ordering and define function call delta framing. Added START_CALL/END_CALL events to contract.
2025-02-18 - Priya Singh (Engineering Lead): Performance targets updated after kernel scheduling experiments; embeddings P95 adjusted from 200ms to 250ms for conservative staging baseline.
2025-02-19 - DevEx Review: requested explicit migration shim for legacy SDK; added migration docs task and estimate.
2025-02-21 - Security: preliminary review done, two medium findings (KMS audit logging gaps, tenant-metadata header hardening). Security team to validate remediations by 2025-02-28.
2025-02-25 - PM: Added launch checklist items for billing and quota header validation per finance request.
2025-02-28 - Arjun Patel: Integration tests for function calls pass in staging; streaming deltas validated against contract. Marking PRD ready for final review.
(To be done) - Schedule executive go/no-go on 2025-03-10 after GA smoke runs
dependencies: ENG-3821 - Runtime: streaming + function call kernel plumbing
ENG-3952 - Observability: token-level cost attribution pipeline
ENG-4010 - Billing: per-token meter and invoice generation
ENG-4123 - Quotas: rate limit header standardization
PM-16801 - Docs: SDK quickstarts and migration guide (coord)
risks: Performance regressions on quantized models could breach latency SLOs - mitigation: limit quantized models for GA and document tradeoffs
Customers with heavy tool-calling patterns may see higher errors during function call streaming - mitigation: create client backoff guidance and a monitoring alert
Incomplete telemetry coverage could delay detection of regressions - mitigation: require Console dashboards before GA and synthetic jobs prior to rollout
Security findings late in cycle can delay launch - mitigation: prioritize fixes and prepare limited GA with enterprise opt-in only
open_questions: Should rerank support per-candidate metadata passthrough in the initial GA or be delayed to post-GA? (ENG input needed)
What is the exact fallback policy surface in headers—should we expose automatic model substitution or require explicit client opt-in?
Do we permit server-side prompt trimming for very long chats by default, or fail with 413 and provide tooling to truncate?
Is async job mode for very long completions a soft launch feature or must it be GA for initial customers?
